Separate the checkpoint load out of TabDPTEstimator.__init__

commit.message:
Separate the checkpoint load out of TabDPTEstimator.__init__

TabDPTEstimator.__init__ downloads or reads the checkpoint and builds
self.model inline, with no way for a caller to reuse an already-built
network across several estimators (a bagged ensemble that fits eight
of them from the same checkpoint currently rebuilds it eight times) or
to substitute one for testing. _load_model() is the same steps as a
separate method the constructor calls once, so a subclass or a
monkeypatch can override it to hand back a cached module instead of
rebuilding one, matching the shape of TabDPTEstimator.to() and other
estimators' load hooks.

While extracting it: clip_sigma and model_weight_path were read as
local constructor variables and never stored on self, so
TabDPTEstimator(...).get_params() raised AttributeError for every
instance (sklearn's BaseEstimator contract requires every constructor
argument to be readable back off self). Both are now stored, which
_load_model reads instead of closing over the constructor's locals.

No public behavior changes: the constructor's signature, defaults and
validation are unchanged, and the existing test suite passes unmodified.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Update BarDistribution class documentation for clarity on logits shape

Revised the documentation for the BarDistribution class methods to clarify the shape of the logits parameter and the expected output shapes. The changes enhance understanding of how independent distributions are indexed, improving overall code readability and usability.

Improve BarDistribution class documentation with clarification on argmax behavior

Added a comment in the BarDistribution class to clarify that the argmax function returns the lowest-index bin when multiple bins share the maximum density. This enhancement improves code readability and understanding of the mode calculation process.

Enhance quantile handling in TabDPTRegressor

Updated the TabDPTRegressor class to include a default set of quantiles for output predictions. Moved validation for ensuring all provided quantiles are floats between 0 and 1 and default value handling to be within the _logits_to_outputs function for better clarity. This change improves usability by simplifying the quantile input process while maintaining robust error handling.

Refactor prediction accumulation in TabDPTRegressor

Updated the prediction accumulation logic in the TabDPTRegressor class to streamline the process. Replaced the use of an intermediate variable with a cumulative sum for logits, enhancing code clarity and performance. This change simplifies the prediction calculation while maintaining the same functionality.

Update README and enhance BarDistribution class documentation

Enhanced the BarDistribution class documentation with detailed descriptions for methods such as mean, median, mode, and sample, improving clarity on their functionality and expected inputs/outputs. Separated regression example into the original point estimate and a new regression probabilistic example to demonstrate the model's capabilities in handling various output types. Updated README to reflect on new exmaple scripts.

Enhance regression example with interval calibration and sharpness metrics

Updated reg_example.py to include calculations for interval coverage and interval scores at specified quantile levels (90, 95). Added new print statements to display sharpness and coverage metrics based on the predictive histogram, improving the demonstration of the model's performance in quantile regression tasks. This is used to demonstrate how a subset of the ScoringBench evaluations are now compatible with the regression API.

Enhance regression example with additional predictive statistics

Updated the regression example in reg_example.py to include calculations for median, mode, and quantile predictions using the TabDPTRegressor. Added print statements to display R2 scores for these estimates, as well as shapes and keys for the full distributional output. This improves the demonstration of the model's capabilities in handling various output types.

Add BarDistribution class and update TabDPTRegressor

Introduced the BarDistribution class for handling distributions over binned continuous targets. Updated TabDPTRegressor to utilize BarDistribution for regression outputs, including mean, median, mode, and quantiles. Enhanced output handling with new output types and improved initialization for constant target scenarios. Updated __all__ exports in __init__.py to include new output types.

Always use inf_batch_size during inference, even without retrieval

Ensures we don't OOM on very large test sets. Downside is that it'll
slow down inference when retrieval isn't used.

Also use inf_batch_size on CPU when explicitly specified, and warn user
to set it explicitly instead of silently overriding with a really low
and slow value (this has made it look unexpectedly slow for me when
testing on CPU before).

commit.message:
Align n_ensembles handling between classifier predict functions

Allows using TabDPTClassifier.ensemble_predict_proba as a single entry
point for probabilistic outputs, matching the behaviour of predict().
This will affect inference behaviour slightly, but only slightly for an
unusual case (using ensemble_predict_proba with n_ensembles==1 will no
longer shuffle columns)

For a future major update, we could consider exposing this behaviour for
predict_proba, more closely matching sklearn expectations, but it might
be too risky a change for existing code.
